subject: physics_2
question_text: Distinguish between half wave and full wave rectifier?

mark_split.label: Half wave rectifier — its five points
Full wave rectifier — its five points

verification.note: The 2+2 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the book prints 'One p-n jnction diode is used' and 'the freuqency of applied A.C'; both are spelled correctly here. Physics hand-checked: number of diodes 1 against 2; one half cycle against both; maxima 4/π² = 40.6% and 8/π² = 81.2%; and the ripple frequency, which is the frequency f of the supply for the half wave rectifier and 2f for the full wave rectifier — the book states this as the number of d.c. pulses per second and it is correct in both rows.

recall_prompt: Compare the two rectifiers point by point — diodes used, half cycles used, efficiency, and pulses per second.

steps.label: Half wave rectifier
lines: 1) One p-n junction diode is used.
2) Only one half cycle of the input a.c.

lines.text: signal is converted into d.c. output.

lines: 5) The number of d.c. pulses per second

lines.text: equals the frequency of the applied a.c.

steps.margin_note: Two marks. Five numbered points; the diode count and the half cycle used are the two that always carry marks.
steps.why: A distinguishing question is marked point by point, so the answer has to be written as a numbered list with the SAME points in the same order for both devices. Writing a paragraph makes the examiner hunt for the comparison.
common_mistakes: Writing a paragraph instead of numbered points. The marks are given point by point.
Saying the output is pure d.c. It is a pulsating d.c. — one pulse per cycle.
Giving 50% as the efficiency. The maximum is 40.6%.

recall.must_convey: That the half wave rectifier uses one diode, rectifies one half cycle, has a maximum efficiency of 40.6%, and gives one pulse per cycle.
accept: one diode and one half cycle
maximum efficiency forty point six per cent
pulses per second equal the supply frequency

steps.memory_tip: Half wave: one diode, one half cycle, one pulse per cycle. Everything is one.

steps.label: Full wave rectifier
lines: 1) Two p-n junction diodes are used.
2) Both the positive and the negative

lines.text: half cycles are converted into d.c.

lines: 5) The number of d.c. pulses per second

lines.text: is twice the frequency of the a.c.

steps.margin_note: Two marks. The same five numbers, in the same order, so the comparison reads across.
steps.why: Both half cycles reach the load, so twice as much charge arrives in each cycle. That single fact explains every other row: twice the pulses, twice the constant on top of the efficiency, and therefore twice the maximum efficiency.
common_mistakes: Saying a full wave rectifier always needs four diodes. The centre-tap circuit in this chapter uses two; a bridge rectifier uses four.
Writing the same pulse rate as the half wave rectifier. It is twice the supply frequency.

recall.must_convey: That the full wave rectifier uses two diodes, rectifies both half cycles, has a maximum efficiency of 81.2%, and gives two pulses per cycle.
accept: two diodes and both half cycles
maximum efficiency eighty one point two per cent
pulses per second are twice the supply frequency

steps.memory_tip: Full wave: two diodes, two half cycles, two pulses. Everything is doubled.

insider_note: Number the points and keep the same order in both lists — the examiner reads across the two columns, not down one.
